overview: Perenti is an ASX-listed diversified global mining services group headquartered in Perth, Western Australia, formed from the 2018 merger of Ausdrill and Barminco and expanded via the 2023 DDH1 acquisition. The company provides contract underground and surface mining, drilling services, and mining technology/support services to resource companies across Australia, Africa, North America and Europe/Middle East, operating in 12 countries with around 10,000 employees. Gold and copper mining underpin roughly 85% of revenue, and the business is transitioning toward tier-one jurisdictions (Australia, North America) and away from West/Southern Africa exposure.

business_model.summary: Perenti earns revenue from multi-year contract mining agreements (underground and surface), drilling services (production, development and exploration drilling), and value-added mining technology/support services (equipment supply, logistics, technology/data solutions). Contracts are typically multi-year with mine owners, providing a degree of revenue visibility, though volumes and margins flex with client capital programs and commodity cycles. FY26 continuing revenue was $3,338.2m (underlying $3,463.2m including BTP for part of the year), down slightly on FY25 as the portfolio shifted toward Australia and North America and BTP was reclassified as discontinued.

revenue_streams.name: Drilling Services (Ausdrill, DDH1, Ranger, Strike, Swick)
Mining & Technology Services (incl. BTP, Supply Direct, Logistics Direct, idoba)

business_model.customer_type: B2B — large-cap and mid-cap mine owners/operators (e.g., Barrick, Newmont/Nevada Gold Mines, AngloGold Ashanti, Bellevue Gold)
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia 57.3%, West Africa 24.4%, Southern Africa 12.8%, North America 5.1%, Europe/Middle East 0.3% of underlying revenue (FY26); tier-one jurisdictions (Australia + North America) represent 69% of revenue; commodity mix Gold 76.2%, Copper 8.4%, Iron ore 3.6%, Nickel 3.4%, Lithium 0.4%, Other 7.9%.

competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest global underground and surface contract mining providers at scale, and one of the largest global drilling services businesses (via the DDH1/Swick/Ausdrill drilling brands); leading positions in hard-rock underground mining and diversified across commodities, geographies and >20 individual projects.

moat_factors.factor: Scale and technical expertise in underground mining
moat_factors.description: Barminco/AMS brings specialized capability in complex, deep hard-rock underground mining as ore bodies become harder to access, a segment with fewer credible global-scale competitors than surface mining.

Multi-decade relationships with major miners (Barrick, Newmont, AngloGold Ashanti) support contract renewals (e.g., Duketon, Dalgaranga renewals in FY26) and follow-on awards (Fourmile adjacent to Goldrush).
Top project is only 6.7% of revenue and top 20 projects ~71.5%, reducing single-contract risk versus smaller peers.
Leverage down to 0.4x net debt/EBITDA and an expanded $650m syndicated facility give capacity to bid larger/longer contracts that smaller competitors cannot fund.

weaknesses: Contract mining/drilling is a commoditized, price-competitive, low-differentiation service business with thin structural margins (~10% EBIT(A) margin) versus resource owners

Significant historical revenue concentration in West/Southern Africa, a region with elevated sovereign, currency, security and policy risk (e.g., forced exit from Iduapriem, Ghana Manganese Company contract loss)
No proprietary resource ownership — earnings entirely dependent on third-party capital expenditure decisions and contract renewal cycles
Capital-intensive business (heavy mining fleet capex) with lower returns on capital than resource owners it services
Complex portfolio (multiple brands: Barminco, DDH1, Swick, Ausdrill, AMS, BTP, idoba) increases integration and management complexity

growth_drivers: North American expansion — Barminco's $275m Fourmile contract at Barrick's project in Nevada builds on the Goldrush relationship and Swick's long-standing US presence
Large Australian contract wins — Bellevue Gold (~$850m, largest Australian contract), plus Dalgaranga and Duketon renewals/extensions
~$20 billion tender pipeline supporting organic growth options across regions
Portfolio recycling — BTP divestment ($100m) and Iduapriem fleet sale ($30-40m) unlock ~$150m of capital in FY27 for reinvestment in higher-returning contract mining and drilling opportunities
Rising drilling utilization across the five drilling brands (Ausdrill, DDH1, Ranger, Strike, Swick) as exploration and production drilling activity lifts, particularly in H2 FY26
Structural growth in underground mining demand as ore bodies get deeper and harder to access, favoring Perenti's underground expertise
Gold and copper sector capex tailwind from strong commodity prices supporting client investment in mine development
Continued deleveraging (0.4x net debt/EBITDA, lowest since Barminco acquisition) creating capacity for further capital returns or bolt-on M&A
New CEO Vanessa Torres (from May/April 2026) tasked with driving the next growth phase after a multi-year turnaround under predecessor Mark Norwell

business.description: Revenue and contract awards depend on mining companies' capital investment decisions, which are sensitive to commodity prices; a gold/copper price downturn would reduce Perenti's pipeline.

Top project is 6.7% and top 10 ~53.5% of revenue; loss or non-renewal of a major contract (e.g., the forced exit from AngloGold Ashanti's Iduapriem mine in Ghana, or the earlier loss of the Ghana Manganese Company contract, which cost $20-25m of earnings) can be material.

~37% of underlying revenue still comes from West and Southern Africa, exposing the group to sovereign, currency, security, and resource-nationalism risk (e.g., Ghana government policy forcing the Iduapriem exit).

Contract mining and drilling are competitively tendered; competitors like Byrnecut (private, well-capitalized), Thiess/MACA and Macmahon compete for the same tier-one contracts, constraining pricing power.
$29.2m non-cash impairment of idoba goodwill/intangibles in FY26 reflects a technology bet that has not scaled as hoped.

financial.description: Leverage is low (0.4x net debt/EBITDA) and the syndicated facility was recently expanded to $650m on improved terms, but the business remains capital-intensive with ongoing fleet capex needs.
Operations across AUD, USD and African currencies create translation and transactional FX risk; FY26 booked $8.0m of net FX losses, mainly unrealized losses on intercompany loans and tax balances.
FY26 operating cash flow conversion fell to 89% (from 99% in FY25) due to two large customer receipts landing just after year-end, illustrating sensitivity of cash flow to receivables timing.

regulatory.description: Ghanaian government policy changes forced an orderly exit from the Iduapriem mine; similar policy shifts in other African jurisdictions could affect other contracts.

As a mining contractor with ~10,000 employees operating heavy equipment underground and on surface, Perenti faces stringent safety regulation across multiple jurisdictions; the company reported zero fatalities in FY26 but safety incidents remain a persistent operational/reputational risk in this industry.

macro.description: ~76% of underlying revenue is gold-linked and ~8% copper-linked; a sustained decline in gold/copper prices would likely slow client capex and mine development, directly reducing contract mining and drilling demand.
Higher-for-longer interest rates can raise the cost of capital for mining clients, delaying project approvals and expansions that feed Perenti's pipeline.

Labor, fuel, and mining consumables cost inflation, along with mobilisation costs (which pressured Drilling Services margin in H2 FY26), can compress contract margins, particularly on fixed-price work.

execution.description: New CEO Vanessa Torres commenced 29 May 2026, succeeding long-tenured Mark Norwell who led the multi-year turnaround and portfolio reshaping; execution risk exists in maintaining strategic continuity and delivering the next growth phase.

BTP divestment (to Beetle Industries, completion expected end of October 2026) and the Iduapriem exit both require successful completion of transaction conditions and redeployment of unlocked capital into accretive growth.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global mining services demand is supported by structural themes: declining ore grades, deeper/harder-to-access deposits favoring underground mining expertise, sustained gold price strength, and growing copper demand tied to electrification/energy transition. Management characterizes the long-term industry outlook as 'very positive' with mining companies increasingly outsourcing to specialist contractors for technical capability and capital efficiency.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical — tied to mining capex cycles and commodity prices, but multi-year contract structures and diversification across >20 projects and multiple commodities/geographies smooth some of the cyclicality relative to a pure commodity producer.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity — higher rates raise clients' cost of capital and can delay mine development/expansion decisions that drive contract awards; Perenti's own leverage is low (0.4x net debt/EBITDA) so direct rate sensitivity on its own balance sheet is limited.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: AUD reporting currency with material exposure to USD (North America, US-dollar denominated African gold contracts) and African currencies; FX losses of $8.0m in FY26 came mainly from unrealized moves on intercompany loans and tax balances.

recent_developments.event: Perenti agreed to divest BTP Group (equipment rental and parts sales) to Beetle Industries (Cratus Group-led consortium) for $100m total consideration ($80m upfront, $20m deferred 12 months); non-cash loss of ~$64m booked in FY26; completion expected end of October 2026; BTP reclassified as discontinued operations.

FY26 results released: underlying revenue $3,463.2m (down 0.8%), record underlying EBIT(A) $339.7m (up 1.9%, margin 9.8%, up 25bps), underlying NPAT(A) $192.1m (up 7.6%); statutory NPAT fell 84.4% to $18.8m due to BTP discontinued-operations loss and impairments; adjusted free cash flow of $182m beat guidance of >$170m; leverage improved to 0.4x net debt/EBITDA, the strongest balance sheet since the 2018 Barminco acquisition; final dividend raised to 4.5cps (7.75cps full year, up from 7.25cps).
Vanessa Torres commenced as Managing Director & CEO, succeeding Mark Norwell who led the company's multi-year turnaround and diversification strategy.

AMS agreed an orderly transition/exit at AngloGold Ashanti's Iduapriem Gold Mine in Ghana, extending services ~6 months while agreeing to sell the on-site fleet for expected proceeds of $30-40m — a forced/managed exit from a West African contract.

Barminco (Contract Mining) secured the $275m Fourmile contract in Nevada (45 months, adjacent to the Goldrush project) and the ~$850m Bellevue Gold underground contract in Australia — the company's largest Australian contract — plus renewals at Duketon and Dalgaranga, reinforcing the strategic pivot toward Australia and North America.

Syndicated debt facility refinanced and expanded from $445m to $650m on improved pricing/terms, oversubscribed with new domestic and international banking partners, extending maturities and liquidity (total available liquidity $911m at year-end).

Non-cash impairments recognized: $25.1m on idle AMS Surface assets (localisation changes) and $29.2m on idoba goodwill/intangibles, reflecting underperformance in the technology segment and African surface asset utilization.

Management guided FY27 underlying revenue of $3.45-3.65bn and underlying EBIT(A) of $335-355m, with FY27 characterized as a 'pivotal year' for growth via ~$150m of capital unlocked from portfolio recycling (BTP, Iduapriem), ramp-up of new contracts (Fourmile, Bellevue) across all regions, and rising drilling utilization; earnings expected to remain second-half weighted; capex guided at approximately $370m.

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO Vanessa Torres described FY27 as a 'pivotal year to drive future growth,' citing the $20 billion tender pipeline, ramp-up of new contracts across all regions, and rising drilling utilization. Management noted FY26 was the fifth consecutive year of underlying EBIT(A) growth since COVID and the fifth consecutive year of meeting market guidance. Earnings are expected to remain second-half weighted in FY27, consistent with historical seasonality.

bull_case: Record underlying earnings for the fifth straight year with FY26 EBIT(A) margin at 9.8% (up 25bps) and NPAT(A) up 7.6%, demonstrating consistent execution and margin discipline through a strategic turnaround

Strongest balance sheet in company history (0.4x net debt/EBITDA, gearing of 12.8%, $911m liquidity) provides capacity to fund the $20bn tender pipeline organically or pursue accretive bolt-on M&A without straining the balance sheet

Active portfolio management (BTP divestment, Iduapriem exit) is unlocking ~$150m of capital to recycle into higher-returning Contract Mining and Drilling Services opportunities while simplifying the group structure

Structural tailwinds from deepening/harder-to-access ore bodies favor Perenti's underground mining expertise (via Barminco/AMS), and strong gold (76% of revenue) and copper (8%) prices are driving client capex and new contract awards (Fourmile, Bellevue)

Deliberate geographic mix shift toward tier-one jurisdictions (Australia + North America now 69% of revenue, up from historically higher Africa weighting) reduces sovereign/political risk profile over time
Consensus analyst ratings are broadly positive (Buy-rated by multiple covering analysts) with price targets raised through 2026 (e.g., to ~A$2.70) implying meaningful upside from current levels
bear_case: Contract mining and drilling remain a low-differentiation, competitively tendered service business with structurally thin margins (~10% EBIT(A) margin), leaving Perenti as a price-taker versus its mining-company clients

Continued exposure (~37% of revenue) to West/Southern Africa carries elevated sovereign, currency and policy risk, evidenced by the forced exit from AngloGold Ashanti's Iduapriem mine in Ghana and the earlier loss of the Ghana Manganese Company contract

Earnings are entirely dependent on third-party mining capex decisions and commodity prices (76% gold-linked); a sustained pullback in gold/copper prices or mining investment would directly compress the contract pipeline and utilization

FY26 statutory net profit collapsed 84.4% to $18.8m (versus underlying NPAT(A) growth) due to the BTP discontinued-operations loss ($64.4m) and non-cash impairments ($54.3m combined on AMS Surface assets and idoba), underscoring that reported statutory earnings can diverge sharply from the underlying/adjusted story management emphasizes

New CEO transition (Vanessa Torres from May 2026) introduces execution/continuity risk just as the company embarks on its next growth phase and larger, longer-duration North American contracts (Fourmile) ramp up

FY27 guidance of flat-to-modest EBIT(A) growth ($335-355m vs FY26's $339.7m) alongside a step-up in capex (~$370m) suggests near-term free cash flow could be pressured even as revenue and earnings guidance imply limited organic growth
